description: Manage SYSTEMS: named groups of up to 9 of your apps, handled as one (ADR-0353). action='list' (default) shows your systems and their apps. 'create' needs `name` and optionally `apps` (dropIds you own, each with an optional short `alias`). 'add' / 'remove' put one app in or out (`systemId`, `dropId`). 'rename' takes `name`. 'delete' removes the grouping only: the apps stay, untouched. A system whose owner deleted it WITH its apps from the dashboard shows `suppressionDemandeeLe`: its apps are offline, kept 30 days, then erased; only the dashboard restores or erases it, and every other action on it is refused. 'delegate' grants `email` (an existing Dropyour account) the role 'mainteneur' on EVERY app of the system, with the same limits as dropyour_delegate. 'label' sets a PRIVATE client label (`client`, empty to remove) used to group systems; the client never sees it. 'export' returns systeme.json: the system in the manifest format (apps with their private routes and events, call permissions with their contracts, subscriptions), where to get each app's content (its own export), the links to apps outside the system, whether shared identity is on, and what is missing (`complet`); it replays with plan/apply once each app's content is added. 'shared_identity' (`enabled`: true or false) makes the apps of this system see the SAME identifier for the same signed-in visitor (app.visitor.id), instead of one per app (the default); the visitor is told on the sign-in page which other apps recognise them; never a shared cookie, and the email still reaches an app only with the visitor's consent for that app. Turning it on or off changes the identifiers apps see (signed-in visitors sign in again); an app that leaves the system goes back to its own identifier. 'view' returns the system with its call permissions (internal or not, verified or not), the last compatibility verdict of each called app, and its dated activity, including apps that left it. 'transfer_link' returns a one-time link (24 h; a new one cancels the previous) to whoever opens it while signed in; `apps` limits it to some of its apps (the others stay with you, in a system of the same name). Links between the apps that leave survive, links to apps outside it are cut, every management token is reset. 'private_routes' (with `dropId`, a server app, and `routes`) reserves paths to the apps allowed to call it: anyone else gets 404, the request never reaches the app; the manifest accepts the same as `apps.<alias>.routesPrivees`. Events (ADR-0368): `apps.<alias>.sujets` = { topic: [keys] } on a server app, and a top-level `abonnements: [{ sujet, de, vers, route }]` (de emits, vers receives on its route; requires the link de→vers, declared in `liens` or already set); applied after the links, nothing is removed by omission. 'plan' and 'apply' take a `manifest` describing the whole system (apps with their html or zip, call permissions with their contracts): plan says, before anything is done, what will be created, published or linked, what is already up to date, what is kept because the manifest does not mention it, and what is refused and why; apply does it step by step (versions saved first on server apps, called apps published before their callers, every new contract replayed at once) and stops at the first failure with a report that never claims more than was done. Running apply again with the same manifest resumes, then does nothing. The manifest never makes an app a server app (that is a subscription) and never deletes anything. An app belongs to one system at most. A system never spans two accounts. Requires a connected account (no managementToken).

alias.description: A short lowercase alias for the app inside the system (e.g. "crm").

client.description: For label: a private client label (empty string removes it).

email.description: For delegate: the email of the other person's Dropyour ACCOUNT.

enabled.description: For shared_identity: true = the apps of this system see the same visitor identifier; false = each app its own (the default).

manifest.description: For plan/apply: { v: 1, systeme: { nom, client? }, apps: { <alias>: { html | zipBase64, nom? } }, liens: [{ de, vers, contrat?: { routes: [{ path, method?, expectStatus?, responseSchema? }] } }], abonnements?: [{ sujet, de, vers, route }] }. The system is matched by its name in your account.

routes.description: For private_routes: paths only apps allowed to call this one can reach (exact /admin or prefix /api/*); an empty list removes them.

name: dropyour_system
title: Group my apps into a system
